quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let other cars merge safely.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the same speed as other traffic on the freeway.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by driving safely and responsibly.

questions.question: When driving down a long or steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors for speeding traffic behind you.
Assume all traffic is maintaining a consistent speed.
Hold down your brake pedal to control the speed of surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for speeding traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when driving down hills. Vehicles, especially large trucks and buses, can speed up on downhill grades. Stay alert for vehicles approaching quickly from behind.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be pushed backward. Press yourself against your seat and keep your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if your vehicle skids. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection where you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see traffic coming from both directions.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look when driving?

options.text: Four seconds ahead
Seven seconds ahead
10 seconds ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 seconds ahead
questions.explanation: Look at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to stop or change lanes if needed. It helps you drive safely, use less fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or a siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to all emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a change in road direction or a narrowing of the road. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: You are parked facing uphill on a street with a curb. You set the parking brake. What should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked uphill on a street with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. When parked uphill without a curb or parked downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: You are driving on an interstate. Traffic is merging onto the highway from an on-ramp on your right. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead on an interstate, move to the left lane when it is safe. This gives merging traffic room to enter the highway.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to drive through before the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means stop if you have not entered the intersection. Stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: When you park your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure one rear wheel touches the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Keep the front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake and leave your vehicle in park when parked on a hill. If there is no curb, turn the wheels so the car rolls away from the road center if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when heading downhill, or away from it when heading uphill.

questions.question: How close can you park to a fire hydrant?

options.text: 15 feet
20 feet
30 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the other car without requiring hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: Another driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed so the tailgater will drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then speed back up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed so the tailgater will drive around you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road intersects ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road intersects ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a side road will intersect with the main road ahead.

questions.question: When is the road surface most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain is just beginning.
After one to two hours of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain is just beginning.
questions.explanation: The road is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with the water to create a slick film.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening around your vehicle. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you see problems early and change your speed or position safely.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road or pavement edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly steer back onto the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the road or pavement edge, do not turn back immediately. Instead, slow down, check for traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter the intersection when safe.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down to a safe speed and cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stalled out of sight. Adjust your speed so you can stop if necessary when approaching a hill or curve.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for potential hazards. Do not just stare at the road in front of your vehicle. Stay alert to all vehicles around you.

questions.question: Getting ____ points on your license within 12 months will result in your license being suspended.

options.text: 15 points
10 points
8 points

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 points
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, certain driving offenses add points to your license. If you get 15 or more points within 12 months, your license will be suspended. The length of suspension depends on how many offenses you have committed.
